Title: My Ego Sabotaged My Writing: A Candid Confession

Illustration by Fresh Idea

Full manuscript in two months. That was the goal. I was on vacation in Mexico, no less, when I checked my email and saw the opportunity. It was mid-June and the conference was happening near the end of August. Perfect timing, I thought, for a writer like me who thrives under pressure.

But as I sat on the sun-soaked beach, sipping margaritas and watching the waves crash ashore, the gnawing voice of my ego started its insidious whisper. "You can do this," it said, "You're a brilliant writer. You've conquered novels, essays, and poetry. This conference will be a breeze."

I allowed myself to believe it. I basked in the glow of my own self-importance, imagining the accolades, the applause, the respect that would come with winning this prestigious contest. I let my ego convince me that I was superior, that I was invincible.

Back at home, I started writing. Every day, I sat at my desk for hours, fingers flying over the keyboard, pouring my heart and soul into the words. I was unstoppable, invincible, a force to be reckoned with.

And then, suddenly, I wasn't.

I hit a wall. The words stopped coming. The once-sparkling prose now read as dull and lifeless. I was stuck, and my ego, in its infinite wisdom, had no solution.

I began to panic. The deadline was approaching, and I was nowhere near finished. I tried to force the words, to will them into existence, but they wouldn't come.

The ultimate question most people have in life is, “what should I do?” This question more accurately translates into, “what kind of profession do I want?”, or “what kind of life do I want to lead?” We’re not just seeking jobs or careers, but rather a meaningful path that aligns with our passions, values, and aspirations.

In a world that's constantly evolving, it can be challenging to find the answer to this question. We're bombarded with societal expectations, peer pressure, and the lure of financial success. However, it's essential to remember that the path to personal fulfillment often lies off the beaten track.

To find the answer to the ultimate question, we must first understand ourselves. What are our strengths? What are our weaknesses? What are our interests? What values do we hold dear? Answering these questions can guide us towards professions and lifestyles that suit us best.

Once we have a better understanding of ourselves, we can start exploring various options. This exploration should not be limited to traditional careers. The rise of the gig economy, remote work, and entrepreneurship offers countless opportunities to create a unique and fulfilling life.

However, the journey to finding the answer to the ultimate question is not always smooth. There will be setbacks, doubts, and fears. But it's important to remember that these are just stepping stones on the path to discovery.

title: Being My Own Advocate: A Journey of Self-Discovery Through Creative Writing

Zion National Park in Utah. Picture taken by yours truly.

Every photograph I take, every written word I craft, is a reflection of my journey—a journey that started with learning to love myself. Creative writing, in particular, has become a powerful tool in this self-discovery process.

In the vast expanse of Zion National Park, where the towering cliffs meet the azure sky, I find a mirror of my own soul. Just as the park's beauty unfolds layer by layer, my thoughts have become more apparent through the art of writing.

Being my own advocate, my own cheerleader, has been a transformative experience. It's a journey that began with a simple question: Who am I? The answer, as it turns out, is not as straightforward as one might think.

Writing has been my compass, guiding me through the labyrinth of self-doubt, fear, and uncertainty. It has provided a platform for me to express myself, to explore the depths of my emotions, and to understand my dreams and aspirations.

Through the words I put on paper, I have learned to see myself more clearly. I have come to appreciate the complexities of my personality, the strengths that I once dismissed, and the vulnerabilities that I once feared. I have learned to love myself, flaws and all.

Being my own advocate also means standing up for my rights, my needs, and my dreams. It means learning to assert myself in a world that often tries to silence women, to tell us that our voices don't matter. But I have found that my voice matters, and it's my responsibility to use it.

Title: Your Punctuality is Reflecting More Than You Know

Life is anything but predictable. People will argue the validity of free will until the end of time. One thing remains to be true though. So much of life boils down to how you react to it.

I like to think that being proactive is a testament to one's character, a silent yet powerful reflection of one's values and principles. One of the most basic yet profound expressions of proactiveness is punctuality.

Punctuality is not just about respecting other people's time; it is a mirror that reveals a multitude of traits. It shows that you are dependable, responsible, and respectful. It demonstrates that you value the commitments you make and the people you commit to.

Moreover, punctuality is a sign of self-discipline. It shows that you have control over your time, and that you are capable of organizing your life in a way that allows you to meet your obligations promptly. In today's fast-paced world, where distractions abound and time is a precious commodity, punctuality stands out as a testament to one's discipline and focus.

But punctuality is not just about the external perception it creates. It is also about the internal benefits it offers. Being punctual instills a sense of purpose and a drive to accomplish tasks on time. It fosters a mindset that values efficiency and productivity, and it encourages the development of habits that lead to success.

In the grand scheme of things, punctuality may seem like a small thing. But the truth is, it is a small thing that can make a big difference.

Title: The Virtue of Muddling Through: Embracing Pragmatism in Pursuit of Knowledge

In the grand tapestry of philosophical thought, few theories have been as influential, yet underappreciated, as pragmatism. Coined by American philosopher William James, pragmatism serves as a refreshing antidote to the traditional, idealistic quest for absolute truth. It temporalizes knowledge and shifts the focus from the abstract pursuit of absolute truth to the tangible achievements of human powers and practices.

Pragmatism advocates for a practical, action-oriented approach to acquiring knowledge. Rather than searching for a static, unchanging truth, pragmatists argue that truth should be understood as a dynamic, fluid concept, continually shaped and reshaped by our experiences and the outcomes of our actions. In the words of James, "The true is the name of whatever proves itself to be good in the way of belief, and good, too, for definite and assignable reasons."

This approach, often encapsulated by the phrase "muddling through," has profound implications for how we navigate the complexities of life. It acknowledges that our understanding is often imperfect, that we make mistakes, and that our beliefs may evolve over time. Yet, it also instills a sense of confidence, encouraging us to act, learn, and grow in the face of uncertainty.

In a world increasingly characterized by rapid change and complexity, the virtue of muddling through takes on a new significance. It allows us to tackle problems that defy simple solutions, to adapt and learn as new information emerges, and to find pragmatic, effective solutions that work within the context of our practical realities.

Moreover, muddling through fosters resilience and flexibility.

Title: Create a Commute If You Work from Home! Fake it for a Balanced Life

In the digital age, the traditional nine-to-five office job has been revolutionized by remote work. Embracing the convenience and comfort of working from home has become the norm for many. However, as we transition from the hustle and bustle of the office to the comfort of our living rooms, there's a crucial aspect of our workday routine we might be inadvertently neglecting: the commute.

Fake it!

Throughout my early twenties, I worked in the hospitality industry. Sometimes it was part-time while studying and other times it was full-time. Regardless of the hours, there was one constant - the commute. Whether it was a bus ride, train journey, or a walk, that daily commute served as a buffer zone between my personal and professional life, providing a much-needed transition.

The Benefits of a Virtual Commute

1. Mental Preparation: A commute, virtual or otherwise, helps us mentally switch from our personal lives to work mode. It's that period of time where we prepare ourselves for the day ahead, allowing us to approach our work with focus and clarity.

2. Separation of Spaces: Working from home can often blur the lines between our personal and professional lives. A virtual commute can help create physical and mental separation, making it easier to draw boundaries between the two domains.

3. Daily Exercise: Even if it's just a walk around the block, a virtual commute can provide a small amount of daily exercise.

Title: Embracing the Future: 15 Tips for Navigating the Crypto and Blockchain Realm

Pictured with the Founders of TokenFest and four phenomenal women in blockchain, I’ve been in San Francisco for a week, immersed in the dynamic world of Crypto and Blockchain. The city is alive with the energy of innovators, investors, and venture capitalists who are shaping the future. Here are 15 essential tips to help you kickstart your own journey into this burgeoning industry.

1. Start by educating yourself: Read books, articles, and whitepapers, and attend webinars and workshops. Resources like "The Internet of Money" by Andreas M. Antonopoulos are a great starting point.

2. Understand the basics: Familiarize yourself with concepts like public and private keys, smart contracts, and consensus mechanisms such as Proof of Work (PoW) and Proof of Stake (PoS).

3. Identify your interest: Decide whether your focus will be on investing in Cryptocurrencies, developing Blockchain solutions, or using Blockchain for various applications.

4. Stay up-to-date: Keep an eye on the latest developments in the industry by following reputable news sources like CoinDesk, Cointelegraph, and Decrypt.

5. Join online communities: Participate in forums and social media groups dedicated to Crypto and Blockchain, such as Reddit's r/CryptoCurrency, and connect with like-minded individuals.

Title: Finding Solace in the Three Refuges: How Buddhism is Guiding Me Through the Coronavirus Outbreak

I don’t consider myself a Buddhist, but I recite what are called the “three refuges” after meditating each morning. I even have them tattooed on my arm along with a fourth. These simple words – Buddha, dharma, and sangha – have become my beacons of hope and peace amidst the chaos of the ongoing coronavirus outbreak.

The first refuge, Buddha, signifies the enlightened one who discovered the path to liberation. In these trying times, I find solace in his teachings, reminding me that suffering is an inherent part of life, but it need not define me. By understanding the nature of suffering and learning to let go, I can find peace and tranquility even in the face of a global pandemic.

The second refuge, dharma, represents the teachings of Buddha. During this outbreak, I turn to the dharma for guidance on navigating fear, uncertainty, and loss. The Eightfold Path serves as a compass, helping me to cultivate wisdom, ethical conduct, and mental discipline. By mindfully following this path, I strive to live a life of purpose and compassion.

The third refuge, sangha, symbolizes the spiritual community. Though social distancing measures have necessitated physical separation, I am grateful for the virtual sangha that has connected me with others who share similar values and aspirations. Through online meetings, discussions, and practices, I feel supported and uplifted in my spiritual journey.

The fourth refuge, a concept often overlooked, is my own self.
